paragraphs: A Class I recall of Imperio Fuego Beef Jerky is underway after the product was produced without inspection [1]. The 2 oz. sealed bags were distributed in Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, and Wisconsin; consumers should not eat this product [1].

Taylor Farms is recalling H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad kits due to undeclared soy and almonds, which may cause serious reactions in people with allergies to these allergens [2]. HAIFA SMOKED FISH is recalling approximately 560 pounds of Cold Smoked Sprats because of potential contamination with Clostridium botulinum, a bacterium that can cause life-threatening illness; consumers should not use the product even if it looks or smells normal [3]. WinCo Foods is recalling WinCo Foods Brand Hoagie Rolls for undeclared sesame [5], and Natural Grocers is recalling Natural Grocers Brand Organic 2-Pound Mung Beans due to potential glass contamination [4].

The FDA has declared an outbreak linked to Trader Joe's chicken wraps over [6]. Five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection have been confirmed in San Luis Obispo County, California, with a suspected link to Brookshire Farms during October 16-26 [15].
